Burns Night Supper

Burns Night Supper Celebration

Celebrate the life and poetry of Robert Burns with a traditional Scottish Burns Night Supper, filled with classic dishes, heartfelt toasts, and lively music.

  1. Early Evening / 6:00 pm

    Welcome and Gathering

    Invite guests to arrive dressed in kilts or tartan to set the festive mood. Begin with a dram of smoky single malt whisky to honor Scottish heritage.

    Recipes: Single Malt Whisky

  2. 6:30 pm

    Cock-a-Leekie Soup Starter

    Serve a warm bowl of traditional Cock-a-Leekie Soup to start the meal, a comforting dish that sets the tone for the feast.

    Recipes: Cock-a-Leekie Soup

  3. 7:00 pm

    Piping in the Haggis

    Have the host, dressed in kilt, pipe in the haggis with ceremony. This marks the highlight of the evening and honors Burns' famous poem.

    Recipes: Traditional Scottish Haggis

  4. 7:15 pm

    Address to the Haggis

    Deliver the traditional Address to the Haggis with passion and flourish, celebrating Burns' wit and Scottish pride.

  5. 7:30 pm

    Main Course: Haggis with Neeps and Tatties

    Serve the haggis alongside neeps (turnips) and tatties (potatoes), classic accompaniments that complete the hearty meal.

    Recipes: Traditional Scottish Haggis · Neeps and Tatties

  6. 8:15 pm

    Toasts and Laddies and Lassies

    Offer toasts to the lassies and the laddies, sharing stories or poems to celebrate friendship and Burns' legacy.

    Recipes: Single Malt Whisky

  7. 8:45 pm

    Dessert: Cranachan and Oatcakes

    Enjoy a traditional Scottish dessert of Cranachan paired with oatcakes, a sweet and crunchy finish to the meal.

    Recipes: Cranachan · Traditional Scottish Oatcakes

  8. 9:15 pm

    Ceilidh Dancing and Singing

    End the evening with lively ceilidh dances and sing 'Auld Lang Syne' to honor friendship and the enduring spirit of Burns Night.

Conclude your Burns Night with warm memories and the timeless words of Robert Burns echoing in your hearts.
